title: Partial recursive functions: search and divergence

based_on.title: Computability and Incompleteness
based_on.pages: 9 (§1.2, partial functions); 33–35 (§2.5, strict partial operations, minimization and recursive functions; version 2007-01-09)

summary: Allow searches to run without a bound, keeping track of exactly when an output exists and when an earlier computation blocks the search.
abstract: To undo doubling, test successive natural numbers until doubling a candidate gives the input. This search finds an answer on even inputs and runs forever on odd ones, illustrating why computations are described by partial functions, which permit inputs with no output. Extending composition and primitive recursion to partial functions, then adding unbounded sequential search, defines the partial recursive functions. The search order matters: a later successful candidate is reached only when every earlier test finishes and rejects its candidate. For tests that always finish, search returns the least witness exactly when one exists; a proof that every input has a witness then proves totality. This separates specifying a search procedure from establishing that it always returns an answer.
